definition: The default register of machine prose: affable, tidy, featureless; the sound of no one in particular.
etymology: From beige (French; originally the colour of undyed wool) + voice. Undyed is precisely the point.
in_use: The first draft always arrives in beigevoice. The craft is dyeing it.
the_case: ‘It sounds like AI’ is an accusation without coordinates — it condemns the whole text and locates nothing. Beigevoice gives the fault an address: not the content and not the grammar, but the register, and a register can be worked on. The accusation becomes an instruction — find the beige, choose the dye. And it protects the innocent, because the register that offends no one belongs to no one: the mean of all voices is no voice, the way the mean of all colours is a warm grey.
seo_title: beigevoice — why AI writing sounds like no one at all
seo_description: “It sounds like AI” is an accusation without coordinates. Beigevoice names the fault: machine prose’s default register, the sound of no one in particular.
